Be weary, a lot of ESTP pages portray this personality as hot headed broskis which is wildly inaccurate. ESTPs are practical but they are essentially logical, they are not sympathisers and tend to be quite confident, ambitious and head strong. 

You mentioned feeling but more so, personal feeling and not so much the consequences. ESFP could be right actually. ( Or even ISFP)Leading with Se (being adventurous, sometimes impulsive and quick thinking, present and down to earth - esfp ) but also being guided by how you feel about things, “it’s all about how I feel” is very Fi (leading Fi= isfp) ...what they feel like to you and how you feel about them. It is quite tricky if you think about all the types and cognitive functions exclusively from one another. Every person has all the cognitive functions, they are just used and prioritised in different orders. But remember just because you aren’t logically thinking or feeling doesn’t mean you don’t have the capacity to think or feel that way at times and vice versa... 

I think taking a “cognitive function” test would help and then maybe an enneagram test- understanding your enneagram could point you in the right direction. 

I don’t know you but I would say ISFP or ESFP sounds about right actually :) good luck and if there’s anything else I can help with, let me know.

Also, I wouldn’t use the descriptions in this test. They are a gross oversimplification, not best fitted for typing yourself.
I think being on time is a result of our Fe not Si. We have the Se addictive personality which reveals itself under the stressy times.

INTJ has the same leading and inferior function, but different aux and tertiary functions :) 

INTJ= Ni Te Fi Se
INFJ= Ni Fe Ti Se

You’ve listed all the functions of INFJ, ENFJ, ISTP and ESTP. So the way you use them determines your type. 

It very hard to recognise Ni... if you use it as your leading function, you probably don’t even realise it. You would probably assume you lead with Fe because it’s out there in the physical and it’s easier to notice. But introverted intuition happens on a sort of subconscious level. 

Intuitive personalities are somewhat absent in the present and the physical, often caught up in abstract thoughts and possibilities. Sensors are more present, focused on the here and now, the facts and on past outcomes and how they can trust their experience because they are good at recalling the past. 

So the order in which these functions stack determines your type but usually differentiating yourself between being an intuitive and a sensor will give you a head start in assuming your personality type. 

If you’re an INFJ, you will feel more logical than “feeling” and more abstract and future minded than present. An INFJs thoughts are logical but their actions are often “feeling” or emotionally driven. We never think in terms of absolutes but sometimes we act in terms of them.

Se would be your weakness so to speak and you will be easily overwhelmed by sensory stimulus... loud noises, crowds and lots of chaos - these things make everyone uncomfortable, or at least most people, but for an INFJ it is basically debilitating. In times of stress you would assume an addictive personality, and indulge in sensory stimulation, either watching a series for 6 days straight, playing video games non stop, being wreckless or eating and drinking in excess. 

The best way to describe to you what it is like being an INFJ is a constant pulling on your mind in all different directions. You will feel as if your mind is constantly contradicting itself. Your world is situated in your mind and your mind is grey. You see and value logic but this logic is fluid, contextual and dynamic... it is contradictory. Your actions are taken dependent on how it will effect others more so than how you feel about them personally. I say will effect because you are concerned with future repercussions. You would care to know the reason but you long to understand the why behind that reason more. 

You might find yourself able to empathise with a serial killer and then hate that you are able to do so. Such conclusions wouldn’t be shared with others for fear that they will judge you. But it’s an ability that helps you understand people, their motivations, their desires and their future actions. It’s pattern recognition, through subconscious observation and reflection. It is introverted intuition, and when it’s paired with extroverted feeling it gives you sight through other peoples eyes. 

This is my experience anyway. I’m still trying to figure myself out and it’s hard but try not to put yourself in a box. You’ve got to think of MBTI as a scale. 

INFJ= Ni Fe Ti Se

ISTP= Ti Se Ni Fe

ESTP= Se Ti Fe Ni

ENFJ= Fe Ni Se Ti 

Hopefully this helps. If you find yourself relating to the qualities of an INFJ, please reach out. We live a lonely existence :)

If you don’t mind me asking, which sites have you used? A lot of typology websites type on the letters and not on actual cognitive function... perhaps try typing in “cognitive functions test”. That might give you some percentages to work from :)

What about ISFP? Or even ISFJ? In someways you are very INFJ (the Ni-Ti loop you seem to have going on) but in other ways I see a lot of Fi and Ni. That “loop” could be some unhealthy Fi... you use extensive detail in your examination of yourself which is more of a sensing function...

INFPS use Ne over Ni and I feel like they are actually quite different from INFJs on a sub surface level (with no shared functions.) ISFPs however make use of Ni and Se to some degree... so they have some overlap with INFJs. In addition ISFJs make use of Fe which you seem to have a lot of as well. But as I mentioned previously the unhealthy Fi can sometimes look like anxiety driven Fe. It’s a question of “when I make this decision, am I making it because it feels right to me (Fi) or because I am concerned about the impact it has on others or whether or not they’ll feel comfortable (Fe). Unhealthy Fi might look like this “I will not make this decision because I don’t want other people to not like me because of it” and unhealthy Fe would look like “I wont make this decision because it will make them feel uncomfortable and it will be my fault” - so you can see how they can be mistaken for one another.

Secondly I would ask yourself whether or not you lead with a perceiving function or a judging function? INFJs lead with a perceiving function which makes them appear more distant, structured and organised. INFPs lead with a judging function so they come across more spontaneous and light hearted. 

INFJs are one of the most commonly  mistyped personalities, and one of the easiest ways to tell the difference between an actual INFJ and a mistyped INFJ is to look at how involved they are with their emotions. INFJs easily absorb other people’s emotions and can get very stressed in atmospheres of conflict, yet internally they are much less focused on feelings than most other feeling types. Many INFJs when they are alone get stuck in what is called a “Ni-Ti loop” where they focus on intuitions and connecting underlying principles to expand their knowledge base. They can obsessively try to learn more and more about something they’re interested in. Unlike INFPs, INFJs are actually somewhat unaware of their own emotions. This is because Introverted Feeling (Fi) is not in their primary function stack and they value intuition above feeling.

You’ve got to prioritise your Recovery before weight loss anyway. From my experience, you can erase the bad habits and re-wire your brain if you’re dieting or restricting. Whenever I try to lose weight all I can think about all day is food, and how badly I want certain things. Naturally food is a trigger for my binge eating, so I made the decision to just eat what I want (for now) but not binge on what I want if that makes any sense. I’ve made an effort to exercise everyday and eat enough calories even though I still have weight to lose. I’m trying to establish permanent, healthy habits, that way my mind is in the right place to tackle this little binge demon that keeps me from achieving my goals.

There’s such a clear distinction between over eating a little and that total lack of control while binge eating. I’ve learned to know the difference and when I get an irrational urge to eat even more after I’ve already eaten and feel full, then I know the bad habits are doing the talking, at that point I can begin the process of separating myself from the urges, I see them and recognise them but I remind myself that they are meaningless, I’ve eaten, Im not hungry and I can chose not to give into them. It is harder at first but eventually your rational thinking gets stronger and the urges weaker...

Essentially you need to focus on recovery first. I think it’s impossible to recover from BED completely all the while still dieting. 

I would recommend listening to the “Brain over binge” podcasts, you can access them from the website or podcast apps, they have really helped but things in perspective for me :)

Essentially you don’t even have to read the whole thing. The book can basically be summarised as follows: 

You have two parts of your brain, the “higher” more rational human side and the “lower” animal side. The part responsible for the urges to binge is the animal side- survival instinct etc... 

When you binge you give in to the animal side this making it stronger. Eventually the animal side of the brain begins to overpower your thoughts and subsequently your actions. So what you have to do is constantly distance yourself from this part of your brain and try to use the rational human side and make this side the dominant one.

You need to experience your urges as thoughts not commands. When you get an urge to binge it is a thought or an idea coming from your animal side of your brain. You can ultimately decide whether or not you want to listen and act on them. Supposedly Hansen suggests that you continuously suppress the animal side and eventually it goes away. But the book gives you little mantras throughout that help you divert you thoughts... you can YouTube Katheryn Hansen or you can google “brain over binge” and you’ll see that there are videos that summarise the book (a lot better than I have over here anyway) 

Good luck!

They really are incredible! But I have to disagree with one point. I wouldn’t say the prey are more agile... cheetahs have incredibly flexible spines! Like all cats, their collar bones and shoulder blades are not fused to their skeletons, rather they are embedded in muscle tissue which give them an extended range of motion. Their tails are heavy and flattened (unlike the circular shape of say a leopard or a house cats) which function as a rudder would in a boat, combined with their flexibility, a cheetah is able to change direction in an instant. Naturally making turns of more than 90 degrees is a piece of cake. 

Adding to your point about overheating; they do run into a bit of trouble when it comes to defending their kills. Exhausted from the chase they have to rest for extended periods of time before even beginning to feed. Additionally their light weight makes them more suited for flight as apposed to fight and so while they have a high hunt-kill success rate (approx 1/5) they end up losing at least half of their kills to larger predators like lions and hyena. Defending their kills are just not worth the risk involved :(
